worker, member of fleet home (hub box.example.com:4021) · /etc/caramelo/config.yaml ·
  caramelod socket /run/caramelo/caramelod.sock · edge off

A machine with an edge answers ports 80 and 443 for the hostnames its
environments are exposed under: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, certificates
issued and renewed on their own, WebSockets passed through, and several
replicas of a service behind one name with the old ones drained rather than
killed when they are replaced.

Run without a subcommand, this is the edge process itself: systemd starts it
with the sockets root bound at boot, and it is not something to run by hand.
Use 'caramelo edge status' to ask a machine what its edge is doing.

Usage:
  caramelo edge [flags]
  caramelo edge [command]

Examples:
  caramelo edge status
  caramelo edge enable --acme-email ops@example.com
  caramelo edge counts --since 10m
  caramelo edge prune --dry-run


Available Commands:
  ca          Print the machine's internal CA root, to trust it
  counts      Requests, errors and connection failures per hostname and replica
  disable     Turn the edge off for this machine (run as root)
  enable      Turn the edge on for this machine (run as root)
  prune       Remove certificates left behind by an issuer this machine no longer uses
  status      Show the machine's routes, targets and certificates

Flags:
      --config-dir string   directory holding config.yaml (default "/etc/caramelo")
  -h, --help                help for edge

Global Flags:
      --fleet string      fleet to talk to, by its name in the commander config (default: the app's fleet, then the default fleet)
      --json              print machine-readable JSON on stdout
      --machine string    raw ssh target to talk to, for a machine that is in no fleet yet: user@host[:port], or 'local'
      --progress string   how progress is written to stderr: text (default) or json, one event per line

Use "caramelo edge [command] --help" for more information about a command.
